column1: Summary Ranges — given a sorted array of unique ints, return the smallest list of range strings 'a->b' (or 'a' for singletons) that exactly cover all values. Example: [0,1,2,4,5,7] → ['0->2','4->5','7'].
column2: PATTERN: Linear scan tracking current run start. | INSIGHT: Walk forward; close a run when the next element isn't consecutive. | STEPS: 1) ans=[], i=0. 2) While i<n: start=nums[i]; while i+1<n and nums[i+1]==nums[i]+1: i+=1. If start==nums[i]: ans.append(str(start)); else ans.append(f'{start}->{nums[i]}'); i+=1. 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1) extra. | PITFALL: Singletons format as 'a' not 'a->a'.

column1: Merge Intervals — given list of [start,end] intervals, merge overlapping ones; return the merged list. Example: [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]] → [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]].
column2: PATTERN: Sort by start, then sweep. | INSIGHT: After sorting by start, an interval overlaps the previous iff next.start ≤ prev.end. | STEPS: 1) Sort by start. 2) ans=[]. 3) For iv in intervals: if not ans or ans[-1][1]<iv[0]: ans.append(iv); else ans[-1][1]=max(ans[-1][1], iv[1]). 4) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n log n) / O(n). | PITFALL: Use ≤ (not <) for the overlap check — touching intervals usually count as overlapping.

column1: Insert Interval — given a list of non-overlapping sorted intervals and a new interval, insert and merge if needed. Return the result. Example: intervals=[[1,3],[6,9]], new=[2,5] → [[1,5],[6,9]].
column2: PATTERN: Three-phase scan (no sort needed). | INSIGHT: Walk: phase 1 = strictly before new (append as-is); phase 2 = overlapping new (merge into new); phase 3 = strictly after (append as-is). | STEPS: 1) ans=[], i=0, n=len(intervals). 2) While i<n and intervals[i][1]<new[0]: ans.append(intervals[i]); i+=1. 3) While i<n and intervals[i][0]<=new[1]: new=[min(new[0],intervals[i][0]), max(new[1],intervals[i][1])]; i+=1. 4) ans.append(new). 5) While i<n: ans.append(intervals[i]); i+=1. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(n). | PITFALL: Don't re-sort — already sorted gives O(n) instead of O(n log n).

column1: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons — array of [start,end] balloon intervals; an arrow shot at x bursts every balloon containing x; return min arrows to burst all. Example: [[10,16],[2,8],[1,6],[7,12]] → 2.
column2: PATTERN: Greedy interval scheduling by END. | INSIGHT: Sort by end; an arrow at the first balloon's end pops every overlapping balloon; advance past those. | STEPS: 1) Sort by end. 2) arrows=1, end=intervals[0][1]. 3) For iv in intervals[1:]: if iv[0]>end: arrows+=1; end=iv[1]. 4) Return arrows. | TIME/SPACE: O(n log n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Sort by END (not start) — classic greedy scheduling pattern.
